Title: NST Leader: Mental health support for teachers
Article:
The Education Ministry has flagged 691 teachers out of 82,126 scanned across primary and secondary schools as needing urgent mental health care and psychological intervention.
There are three worrying reasons for the  teachers' poor mental health.
Firstly, they are overwhelmed by heavy workloads, toxic school leadership  and increasing digital and administrative demands.
Secondly, they face severe debt and financial challenges, coupled with stressful work performance demands.
Thirdly, they experience harassment from parents, which spurs isolation and hesitation to seek help.
The findings come from recent screenings  based on the ministry's Psychological Well-Being Inventory (IKPsi) framework.   Of the teachers flagged, 636  were at a "moderate" level — their mental reserves were spent due to chronic stress, and they experienced early burnout and persistent emotional exhaustion.
They were given preventive counselling, focusing on stress management and coping mechanisms.
Meanwhile, 32 teachers were categorised as "moderately low" and faced major psychological distress while struggling to cope with high workload, anxiety, sleep disruption and isolation.
Counsellors are helping them cope with crushing debt or toxic workplaces. Finally, 23 teachers categorised as "low" experienced psychological distress, burnout and clinical depression so severe that they can't live and work healthily.
They have been placed under psychiatric evaluation, intensive therapy and medical leave.
This might be a problem: the ministry's IKPsi screening is rolled out in phases, meaning that many teachers were already in poor mental health before screening.
Teachers hide their symptoms and answer "perfectly" on official forms, fearing a bad score would ruin their  performance reviews, affect promotions and grade advancements, and lead to them being labelled as problematic or "weak".
Furthermore, the relatively low number of teachers flagged  suggests an underrepresentation due to how the screening was structured.
A reference to developed nations tells a more desperate situation.
In Australia, 52 per cent of teachers suffer from clinical depression, 35 per cent in the United Kingdom, 79 per cent in the United States, while the global average is 25 to 35 per cent.
These figures suggest that the Education Ministry has only identified teachers already at an acute stage, leaving the much larger group neglected.
Nevertheless, the screening is a positive step towards early detection.   To  tackle the problem, stigma against teachers seeking help must be  removed, and their privacy and confidentiality shielded.
Teachers should not be made to feel ashamed to  ask for help.    Instead, this must be seen as being responsible, not a sign of professional weakness.
With the first step of early identification underway, success will depend on the ministry's  sustained support for  teacher recovery.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Families claim Malaysians held in Taiwan were exploited by scam syndicate
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Three Malaysians detained in Taiwan on suspicion of involvement in fraud activities may have been victims of exploitation by the syndicate, says the Malaysian International Humanitarian Organisation (MHO).
Its secretary-general, Datuk Hishamuddin Hashim, said the claim was based on information and evidence provided by the families of the individuals concerned.
He said the Malaysians were believed to have been forced to carry out the activities, while their passports were allegedly held by the syndicate.
Hishamuddin said MHO had held an official meeting with the Foreign Ministry to discuss the plight of the Malaysians and coordinate efforts to assist their families.
He said information provided by the families raised questions about the individuals' freedom to make decisions and the circumstances that led to their involvement in the activities.
"Based on their families' accounts, the victims are believed to have been forced to withdraw money from ATMs in Taiwan.
"Their passports were also allegedly held by the syndicate, raising serious questions about their freedom to make decisions and the actual circumstances that led to their involvement in these activities.
"The claims that they did not act voluntarily and had no criminal intent, as suspected, must be thoroughly examined to ensure each case is assessed based on the facts and evidence," he said in a statement.
Hishamuddin said MHO believed all information should be thoroughly examined to ensure the circumstances faced by each individual were assessed fairly.
He said any elements of coercion, passport confiscation or exploitation by the syndicate should be investigated thoroughly and taken into account in the justice process.
MHO would work with Wisma Putra and the Malaysian representative office in Taiwan to identify suitable channels of assistance and legal services for the families, he added.
"This cooperation is important to ensure the families receive the necessary information and can explore the legal avenues available to help their respective family members.
"MHO also hopes coordination between the government, the Malaysian representative office in Taiwan and relevant parties will help clarify the circumstances of each case, particularly regarding allegations of exploitation and coercion by transnational criminal syndicates.
"Our priority is to ensure the claims that they were victims of exploitation are thoroughly investigated and each case is assessed fairly based on the evidence and actual circumstances," he said.
International media previously reported that three Malaysians were detained in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, on suspicion of acting as money mules for a scam syndicate.
Central News Agency (CNA) reported that the three male suspects, aged 18, 26 and 39, had entered Taiwan as tourists before being detained separately.

Title: Tuan Ibrahim: CSA must not become political bargaining chip
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional members of parliament do not need to sign a Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) with the government, as their support for the Budget and bills tabled in Parliament should be sufficient.
PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the opposition coalition believed that supporting the Budget and government bills was enough, without having to enter into a formal agreement with the government.
Tuan Ibrahim, who is also Pas deputy president, cautioned against making the CSA a new political culture in the country, particularly if allocations were extended only to MPs who agreed to sign the document.
"The government should respect the people's choice and ensure that allocations are channelled fairly to all constituencies," said the Kubang Kerian MP.
He said the government should not use allocations as an incentive to secure political support, adding that leaders had a responsibility to uphold justice and treat everyone fairly.
Tuan Ibrahim said opposition MPs had continued to support the Budget and various bills tabled by the government, except for the proposed legislation to limit the prime minister's tenure.
He added that even the proposed legislation had not received unanimous support from government MPs.
"We hope the government will reconsider its approach and extend allocations to all MPs to strengthen the country's democratic system," he said.
He also warned against allowing the CSA to become a form of threat or inducement to MPs, particularly when the government was making efforts to combat corruption and bribery.
"We do not want this to become a form of coercion or gratification for MPs," he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the government is
open to signing a CSA
with any opposition member of parliament, not just those from Bersatu.
He said there were no conditions attached to the arrangement, following the signing of an agreement involving 13 MPs yesterday.
Yesterday's agreement involved six Bersatu MPs, Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and six independent MPs who had previously declared their support for Anwar.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof signed the agreement on behalf of the government.

Title: Zahid hopes Malaysia-China ties will continue to strengthen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes Malaysia-China relations will continue to strengthen through closer cooperation that benefits both countries.
In an Instagram post tonight, he said diplomatic ties established in 1974 had fostered growing friendship between the two countries, which was now entering its 52nd year.
Earlier today, Zahid received a delegation at the Malaysia-China Friendship Dinner in Putrajaya, which provided a platform for both sides to exchange views and share the latest developments.
He said the meeting also provided an opportunity to continue discussions following his recent official working visit to Beijing and Tianjin.
"I had the opportunity to discuss many things with the Chinese delegation that was present just now.
"As it happened, I have just returned from my official working visit to Beijing and Tianjin, so there was much to share and follow up on from the meetings that took place there," he said.

Title: Sim: Local businesses must benefit from government, GLC and MNC procurement
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The government wants local content to be given greater consideration in procurement by government agencies, government-linked companies (GLCs) and multinational corporations (MNCs) to create more opportunities for local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim said the approach was aimed at ensuring local businesses benefited from investments and the development of domestic supply chains.
"We also want government procurements, GLC procurements and, of course, MNC procurements to have a perspective for local content. We want foreign direct investment (FDI) to come in to benefit local businesses. So, there must be a requirement for local content," he said.
He said this during a panel discussion with Grant Thornton Malaysia National Tax Practice Leader Datin Seah Siew Yun at the Grant Thornton Tax Seminar on Budget 2027 here today.
Sim said local content requirements were among the components of the Scale Action Plan, which would form the ministry's next phase of longer-term structural reforms for the MSME sector.
He said Scale covered SME redefinition, cash flow protection, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, local content requirements and easier access to financing.
The ministry was looking at implementing the reforms through legislation, regulations or policy, he added.
On FDI, Sim said the government had also revised its investment incentive system under the new incentive framework, with tax incentives linked to key performance indicators (KPIs).
The criteria included creating high-paying jobs for Malaysians and developing local supply chains, with the approach intended to ensure foreign investments generated spillover benefits for MSMEs instead of benefiting only large companies.
Meanwhile, Sim said GLCs and government-linked investment companies (GLICs) had an important role in developing local industries and helping smaller businesses grow, while avoiding crowding them out of the market.
He said the government had instructed GLCs and GLICs to invest up to RM25 billion annually in developing local supply chains, adding that part of the funds should be invested domestically to build local industries.
Sim said strengthening MSMEs was crucial as they accounted for about 96 per cent of business establishments in Malaysia, although their contribution to gross domestic product (GDP) remained below 40 per cent.
The government was targeting MSMEs to contribute at least 40 per cent to GDP, he said, noting that while SMEs also made up the overwhelming majority of business establishments in many developed economies, their contribution to GDP was higher.

Title: Macron's Malaysia visit set to boost bilateral ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: French President Emmanuel Macron is expected to visit Malaysia in less than three weeks, providing an opportunity to strengthen economic and business ties between the two countries.
Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said Macron is expected to visit Malaysia from Nov 16-17.
Sim said the visit would provide fresh impetus for collaboration between Malaysian and French companies, building on decades of commercial relations and growing investment ties.
"President Macron will be visiting Malaysia in about three weeks.
"This is an absolute opportunity to foster relationships between Malaysian companies and French companies," he said at the Malaysia-France gala dinner marking the 35th anniversary of the Malaysian-French Chamber of Commerce and Industry (CCI France Malaysia).
Sim said Malaysia and France have enjoyed more than 350 years of trade ties.
Over 300 French multinational companies and around 600 French business entities are now operating in Malaysia across various sectors.
He cited Airbus and Safran as key players in Malaysia's aerospace ecosystem, while STMicroelectronics has established high-volume manufacturing operations in Johor.
On trade, Sim said negotiations for a Malaysia-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) were progressing, with the latest round of discussions held in Brussels in September.
He said Malaysia had also recently engaged with members of the European Parliament on the proposed agreement, signalling continued momentum in efforts to advance negotiations.
"These are very exciting times for Malaysia and the European Union, especially France. I think this is on the right track and in the right direction," he said.
An FTA with the EU could provide further opportunities to expand market access and strengthen trade and investment flows between Malaysia and European businesses.
Meanwhile, French ambassador to Malaysia Marc Abensour said Macron's upcoming visit would provide a significant opportunity to elevate bilateral relations to the level of a strategic partnership.
He said it would be the first visit by a French president to Malaysia in nearly a decade, following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's visit to Paris in July 2025 and French Minister for Foreign Trade Nicolas Forissier's visit to Malaysia.
Abensour said France and Malaysia were increasingly aligned in their efforts to strengthen economic security and protect critical supply chains amid growing geopolitical uncertainties.
"At the core of this relationship is a partnership for sovereignty. In an era where trade, energy and technology are increasingly weaponised, economic security is paramount.
"We must secure critical value chains to strengthen our mutual resilience," he said.
Abensour said France is now Malaysia's second-largest European investor, with its investment stock growing by 190 per cent over the past decade, he said.
Bilateral trade between the two countries exceeded RM22 billion in 2025, representing an 11 per cent increase, driven partly by a 40 per cent surge in French exports, particularly in aerospace.
He also highlighted Safran's €113 million expansion of its facility in Negri Sembilan, which is expected to double its capacity.
He said French companies had established a significant presence in Malaysia, employing more than 30,000 people and supporting the country's ambition to move up the value chain through high-technology industries and higher-skilled jobs.
Abensour said the presidential visit would also feature a business forum focusing on three strategic areas: digital sovereignty, aerospace and energy transition.
He said both countries could benefit from closer collaboration in developing diversified and resilient energy systems.
"Accelerating the transition to diversified, resilient energy systems is an urgent priority for both our nations, creating tremendous opportunities for French and Malaysian companies to jointly build the industries of tomorrow," he said.
While acknowledging Malaysia's economic resilience and projected growth of around five per cent in 2026 and 2027, he said reliance on crude-related subsidies carried significant fiscal costs.
Accelerating the transition towards diversified and resilient energy systems would therefore create opportunities for companies from both countries to develop new industries and technologies, he added.

Title: Melaka polls: Gen Z wants swift action, solutions – Adly
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan Melaka chairman Adly Zahari has defended the coalition's young candidate for the Kuala Linggi state seat, Mohammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah.
The 25-year-old, better known as Muklis Mubin, has faced allegations of using his connections to the prime minister and misusing funds from the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry.
Adly said Muklis Mubin and PH's Klebang candidate Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir, 26, were among the young faces fielded by the coalition in the Melaka state election.
He said Muklis Mubin had been an active volunteer and was entitled to help the public by working with relevant agencies.
Adly said the candidate's ties with the Prime Minister's political secretary, Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim, stemmed from their friendship within the same party.
"Perhaps he sees potential in everything around him. That is why he is associated with the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry when providing assistance.
"I think all elected representatives have networks, especially those in the government, to help resolve people's problems.
"They (Gen Z) want swift action, responsiveness and the best solutions to community problems," he said in a press conference after the PH Hi-Tea with the Melaka Media Practitioners Club (Pendika).
Also present were acting Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli and Pendika chairman Amir Mamat.
Adly, who is also deputy defence minister, said he supported Muklis Mubin's efforts but had reminded him to be prepared to accept criticism and understand the risks involved in every action.
On the negative perceptions of Gen Z, who are often labelled the "strawberry generation", he said the label should not be used to judge the capabilities of young people.
He said Muklis Mubin and Farzana were examples of educated and knowledgeable young people capable of handling pressure, including criticism on social media.
"I reminded them that winning or losing is secondary. What matters most is their aspiration to serve the people and the community while they are still young," he said.

Title: BYD, Gentari eye Petronas stations for flash charging
Article:
BYD and Gentari are exploring the deployment of ultra-fast EV charging infrastructure in Malaysia, including at Petronas stations and major highway corridors, as the Chinese automaker seeks to expand charging options for its vehicles.
BYD Malaysia and Gentari recently signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) at BYD's global headquarters in Shenzhen to explore bringing BYD flash charging technology to Malaysia, although a rollout timeline and investment details were not disclosed.
The technology is designed to deliver its fastest charging speeds to vehicles equipped with BYD's second-generation Blade Battery.
The Denza Z9GT, one of the first models in Malaysia to support the system, can charge from 10-70 per cent in five minutes and to 97 per cent in nine minutes, according to BYD.
The Z9GT features a 122.49kWh battery and a 1,000-volt electrical architecture.
Existing BYD models can also use the charging infrastructure, but charging speeds will depend on each vehicle's capabilities.
BYD Malaysia managing director Jacob Ma said the collaboration marked a step towards bringing the company's next-generation charging technology to local customers.
As an initial step, the companies will focus on selected Denza luxury showrooms before exploring locations at Petronas stations, intercity routes and highway rest and service areas.
The partnership will also look at developing local capabilities, including training and upskilling technicians to support Malaysia's growing EV ecosystem.
Separately, Denza Malaysia has introduced Fjord Green as a new exterior colour for the Z9GT, joining Rime Gold and Obsidian Black.
The company said more than 100 units of the model had been delivered in Malaysia since its launch.
Priced at RM358,800, the Z9GT produces 850kW, or 1,156PS, and can accelerate from zero to 100km/h in 2.7 seconds.

Title: Melaka polls: MCA gets two additional seats based on winnability – Rauf
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional have allocated two additional seats to MCA for the Melaka election based on winnability and ground assessments, said state BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh.
He said the decision to allocate the Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir state seats to MCA was reached through mutual agreement, with both coalitions recognising that the seats should be contested by the party with the better chances of winning.
The latest allocation brings MCA's total to four seats, while BN will contest 23 seats overall.
"The decision was reached through mutual negotiations and in the interests of both sides, after reviewing the findings of studies which showed that it would be better to allocate the seats to the party with greater potential to win.
"Both sides agreed to hand the seats to MCA. This gives MCA two additional seats, bringing its total to four and BN's overall tally to 23," he told reporters after attending the Tanjung Bidara Constituency's Hi-Tea programme in Masjid Tanah.
Rauf also dismissed claims that the last-minute decision was prompted by political pressure from MCA, saying it had been reached amicably.
He said BN's maturity as a coalition, built on a strong relationship spanning more than seven decades, had enabled seat allocation issues to be resolved through consultation and a family-like approach.
"There is no need to debate this because we have resolved it through a family-oriented approach, and our sense of togetherness has lasted more than 70 years," he said.
Nominations take place tomorrow, with early voting on Nov 10 and polling on Nov 14.

Title: Vandalism caused broken window on KTM Komuter train, says KTMB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A broken window on the Padang Besar-Butterworth KTM Komuter Utara service, which went viral on social media yesterday, was caused by vandalism, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has confirmed.
In a statement today, KTMB said Train No. 2951 was struck by an unidentified object thrown from outside about 6pm yesterday while travelling between Arau and Kodiang, shattering a window on the left side of its second coach.
"KTMB took immediate action after being alerted by the train driver, clearing the affected coach and restricting passenger access to it as a safety measure.
"KTMB auxiliary police personnel were also deployed to help manage passenger movement and ensure the situation inside the affected coach remained under control," it said.
The train resumed its journey at 6.21pm, 21 minutes behind schedule.
The train set was subsequently taken out of service and held at Bukit Tengah Depot for inspection and replacement of the damaged window before returning to passenger service the following day.
KTMB said it had lodged a police report.
It said acts of vandalism against railway assets were taken seriously, warning that throwing stones at moving trains could endanger the lives of passengers and train crew.
Throwing stones at trains is an offence under Section 132 of the Land Public Transport Act 2010 (Act 715), punishable by a fine of up to RM25,000, imprisonment for up to 10 years, or both upon conviction.
Section 128 of the same Act covers offences involving damage to railway property, with penalties varying according to the nature of the offence.
KTMB urged the public to refrain from acts that could endanger railway operations and to alert the authorities if they witnessed suspicious activity.

Title: i‑City's newest residences powered by Nvidia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: i-City is working with TwinMatrix Technologies to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) companion for its planned 500-unit AI Living residential development, targeted for completion in 2030.
Called i-Ris, the digital assistant will use Nvidia's digital-human technology and computing capabilities to help residents interact with their homes and coordinate connected services.
TwinMatrix, an Nvidia Inception company, will use Nvidia ACE technology to develop a lifelike digital avatar designed to communicate naturally with residents.
Nvidia's graphics processing unit computing will support the AI systems that link different home technologies.
The initiative aims to integrate smart-home systems, domestic robots, wellness devices and other services through a single interface.
TwinMatrix founder and chief executive officer Eric Liu said the development would go beyond connecting individual devices.
"We want to create an intelligent environment where residents can interact naturally with their homes, while the underlying systems work together to support their everyday needs," he said.
The planned companion could help residents organise schedules, access information and coordinate household services.
Future applications could include directing domestic robots, adjusting home settings and providing wellness information using authorised wearable-device data.
The system will draw on TwinMatrix's expertise in spatial AI and digital twin technology to connect the different platforms and account for the physical environment in which residents live.
Nvidia's startup and partnership manager for developer programmes in Asia Pacific South Pang Pei Yi said digital-human technology and AI computing could make interactions with connected services more intuitive.
i-City director Datuk Eu Hong Chew said the project would distinguish AI Living from conventional developments.
Development of i-Ris will occur in stages, starting with conversational functions and resident services before expanding into robotics, wellness and smart-home integration.

Title: Lianson adds Malaysia's first DP2 heavy-lift vessel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lianson Fleet Group Bhd (LFG) is expanding its offshore marine capabilities with the acquisition of a heavy-lift vessel capable of handling up to 4,000 tonnes.
This positions the group to pursue larger and more complex offshore projects across Southeast Asia.
Lianson said its wholly-owned Icon Samudera (L) Inc acquired the vessel, which will be renamed LFG Hercules.
Upon completion of its Malaysian registration, the vessel will become the country's first Malaysian-flagged Dynamic Positioning Class 2 (DP2) offshore heavy-lift vessel.
Equipped with a main crane with a lifting capacity of 4,000 tonnes and DP2 technology, the vessel will strengthen Lianson's ability to undertake specialised offshore operations.
The acquisition also opens opportunities in offshore decommissioning, oil and gas infrastructure and renewable energy projects as demand grows for specialised marine services across the region.
Managing director Lim Chern Wooi said the acquisition marked an important step in developing the group into a broader regional maritime player.
He said the vessel would complement Lianson's existing fleet ownership, chartering and offshore support operations, allowing it to pursue larger projects across the offshore energy lifecycle.
Lim added that ageing offshore infrastructure and the gradual development of renewable energy projects presented longer-term growth opportunities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ni Hsin links treasury share sale to stock volatility
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ni Hsin Group Bhd says the resale of five million treasury shares for RM2.38 million may have contributed to the sharp fall in its share price and surge in trading volume.
In its response to Bursa Malaysia's unusual market activity (UMA) query today, the cookware manufacturer said it could not conclusively establish whether the disposal had triggered the recent trading activity.
"While the board is unable to conclusively determine whether the said disposal contributed to the recent trading activity, it may have had an impact on the trading volume and/or share price of the company's securities," it said in a filing.
The shares were resold on Oct 26 at between 47.5 sen and 48 sen apiece, leaving the company with 44.35 million treasury shares.
Ni Hsin said it was unaware of any rumours or reports that could explain the unusual trading, following checks with its directors, major shareholders and other relevant parties.
It also cited two previously announced corporate exercises: its proposed diversification into the electric vehicle (EV) business and a proposed one-for-two bonus issue of up to 312.65 million free warrants.
The company said it remained compliant with Bursa Malaysia's Main Market Listing Requirements, including immediate disclosure obligations.
The UMA query followed a sharp sell-off on Friday.
Ni Hsin shares plunged as much as 59.5 per cent to 15 sen before closing at 26 sen, down 11 sen or 29.7 per cent.
More than 66 million shares changed hands.
The decline came just three days after the stock hit an all-time high of 51 sen on Oct 27.
Ni Hsin shares had surged about sixfold since Aug 20, despite the group reporting a quarterly loss.
The rally continued after its Sept 8 announcement of plans to enter the EV business.
The proposed warrant issue is intended to raise funds for working capital and capital expenditure upon exercise.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal floods: Perkeso payments to next of kin expected on Nov 4 – MASFIH
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) payments to the next of kin of Malaysians who perished in the Nepal-Tibet flood tragedy are expected to be disbursed on Nov 4, according to Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH).
MASFIH coordinator and spokesperson Dr Manivannan Rethinam said several families had been informed of the development by Perkeso, which was expediting the collection of supporting documents to facilitate the payments.
"Following the meeting with the Human Resources Minister on Wednesday, Perkeso began contacting the next of kin of individuals who were eligible for payments yesterday," he said in a statement.
Manivannan said MASFIH had also helped facilitate the process by coordinating contact details of the next of kin after highlighting several communication challenges at the initial stage.
He said the coordination had helped streamline communication and enabled the families concerned to be contacted directly for documentation and payment arrangements.
Meanwhile, MASFIH is still awaiting the government's decision on the special financial assistance for 54 Malaysian families affected by the tragedy.
Manivannan said the organisation hoped the matter would be discussed at the cabinet meeting today and result in a positive decision, followed by an official announcement and concrete measures to assist the affected families.
He said MASFIH would continue working with the authorities and relevant agencies to monitor developments and ensure that the welfare of all affected families continues to be given attention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ab Rauf earns UKM doctorate with research on digital village initiative
Article:
MELAKA: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has completed his Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) through Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's (UKM) Accreditation of Prior Experiential Learning for Qualifications (APEL.Q) programme after 2 years of study.
In a Facebook post today, Ab Rauf said the official Senate confirmation letter was presented to him by UKM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Sufian Jusoh, accompanied by a university delegation, during a visit to his residence in Kampung Pulau, Masjid Tanah, last night.
He said his research, titled Digital Technology Management Among Traditional Village Communities: An Analysis of the Melaka Digital Village Initiative, focused on efforts to harness digital technology among traditional village communities to help them navigate the digital transformation.
"For me, knowledge is not merely about obtaining a degree, but must be translated into benefits and change for the people.
"I dedicate this achievement to the people of Melaka. This is not merely a personal accomplishment, but a tribute to Melaka and my commitment to continuing to strengthen the Digital Village initiative for the people's future," he said.
Ab Rauf also expressed his appreciation to UKM staff, lecturers and the research team for their guidance, support and cooperation throughout his research.
He said the findings would be published in a journal to serve as a reference and source of inspiration for future generations, particularly in advancing the digitalisation agenda among rural communities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bank Rakyat names fintech accelerator winners
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Rakyat has named 11 fintech companies that completed its 2026 Fintech Accelerator Programme (BRFAP 2026), following 79 applications for the initiative.
The programme is organised in collaboration with PlugAndPlay and the Fintech Association of Malaysia (FAOM), with support from Payments Network Malaysia Sdn Bhd (PayNet).
It aims to identify technology solutions for banking operations and customer services.
TNEX Malaysia Sdn Bhd won the grand award, while Unbraided AI Sdn Bhd received the silver award and Carbon AI Sdn Bhd the bronze award.
The other participants were PowerCred Technologies, Dataverse Sdn Bhd, Finology Sdn Bhd, IntelliLabs AI Solution, Codebase Technologies, GBG (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, Vespid Sdn Bhd and Wazzap Me Sdn Bhd.
Bank Rakyat chief executive officer Ahmad Shahril Mohd Shariff said the programme focused on finding fintech solutions to address specific operational challenges in banking, with selected ideas potentially progressing to proof-of-concept evaluation.
"The programme gives fintech companies the opportunity to tailor their solutions to practical banking needs through guidance from industry experts and feedback from banking institutions," he said.
He said the initiative also provided opportunities for Bank Rakyat to work with fintech companies as part of its digital transformation efforts.
Participants underwent orientation sessions, workshops, mentoring, pitch training and industry-sharing sessions before the final assessment.

Title: MAA Group faces going concern warning after RM107mil loss
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MAA Group Bhd has received a warning from its external auditor KPMG regarding significant uncertainty over its ability to continue operating and meet its financial obligations over the next 12 months.
This follows a RM106.9 million loss in its financial year 2026 (FY26), the group said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
MAA said it received an unqualified audit opinion with a material uncertainty related to going concern for the financial year ended June 30, 2026.
KPMG noted that MAA's current liabilities of RM102.5 million exceeded its current assets of RM99.4 million as of June 30, leaving a shortfall of RM3.1 million.
"These conditions indicate that material uncertainties exist that may cast significant doubt on the ability of the group to continue as a going concern and to meet its financial obligations over the next twelve months from the date of the authorisation of these financial statements," KPMG said in its audit report.
An unqualified audit opinion means the financial statements are fairly presented under applicable accounting standards.
However, the going concern warning highlights uncertainty over the group's financial position.
MAA's board believes the financial difficulties are temporary and has outlined several measures to improve liquidity.
These include plans to raise RM139.1 million by disposing of stakes in certain entities outside the group's consolidated accounts, properties and a hotel operation.
The group also expects gross settlements of RM38 million from efforts to recover credit-impaired loans in its financial services business.
In addition, MAA said it secured funding through investment notes issued by a subsidiary and is pursuing further issuances to raise additional funds.
It also cited continued financial support from a substantial shareholder.
Based on these measures, the board maintained that preparing the FY26 financial statements on a going concern basis was appropriate.
MAA was previously involved in a legal dispute with Bursa Malaysia over a proposed disposal of German assets owned by now-delisted KNM Group Bhd, in which MAA was the largest shareholder.
In May, the High Court dismissed Bursa's lawsuit seeking to stop an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) called by MAA to obtain KNM shareholders' approval for the proposed sale of Deutsche KNM GmbH.
Bursa filed the suit in October 2025, arguing that the EGM should not proceed until KNM had complied with the Main Market Listing Requirements.
The court ruled that MAA, as a shareholder, should not automatically bear the full obligations of a listed issuer simply because it had called the EGM under the Companies Act 2016.
MAA held a 19.37 per cent stake in KNM at the time.
The dispute centred on KNM's proposed €270 million (about RM1.26 billion) sale of its German unit to Japan's NGK Insulators Ltd. The deal subsequently fell through.
KNM, classified as a Practice Note 17 company in 2022, had pursued the disposal as part of efforts to restructure its finances and meet debt obligations.
Bursa rejected KNM's regularisation plan in October 2025, and the company subsequently proceeded with its delisting.
KNM has since sued NGK Insulators, seeking damages over the failed transaction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Clear skies expected on nomination morning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Clear skies are expected across all three districts in Melaka tomorrow morning, coinciding with nomination day for the state election.
According to the Malaysian Meteorological Department's (MetMalaysia) website, Jasin, Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah are expected to experience clear weather in the morning, with temperatures ranging from 23 to 24 degrees Celsius.
However, thunderstorms are forecast in Alor Gajah and Jasin in the afternoon, while Melaka Tengah is expected to remain clear.
As of tonight, 189 nomination forms had been purchased, with 45 prospective candidates having paid their deposits.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with nomination day tomorrow and early voting on Nov 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Forest fires affect five Indonesian provinces, floods hit thousands in North Sumatra
Article:
JAKARTA: Forest and land fires have affected 1,410 hectares across five Indonesian provinces, while floods have displaced or affected thousands of households in North Sumatra, prompting continued disaster response operations across the country.
National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) Disaster Data, Information and Communication Centre acting head Berton Panjaitan said South Papua recorded the largest area under firefighting operations, at 502 hectares, based on figures as of 7am local time today.
It was followed by Central Sulawesi with 295 hectares, Southeast Sulawesi (257 hectares), Maluku (182 hectares) and East Kalimantan (174 hectares).
"The pattern has changed considerably. Previously, fires were reported in parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan, and today, we are seeing fires in East Kalimantan, Central and Southeast Sulawesi, Maluku and South Papua," he said in a video briefing.
Berton said 58 aircraft remained deployed for firefighting operations, comprising 23 aircraft for patrol, surveillance and weather modification operations, and 35 helicopters for water-bombing missions.
He added that 23,900 kgs of cloud-seeding materials, including salt and dry ice, had been used in Kalimantan and South Sumatra.
Unhealthy air quality readings were also recorded in Sendawar, West Kutai district, and at three monitoring stations in Nusantara, Indonesia's new capital in East Kalimantan.
Separately, Berton said floods in North Sumatra had affected 7,615 households.
He said seven provinces – Aceh, Lampung, Bengkulu, Riau, West Sumatra, South Sumatra and North Sumatra – were under heightened alerts for heavy to very heavy rainfall.
The weather forecast also indicated the possibility of moderate to heavy rainfall across parts of Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Java, Bali, Maluku, North Maluku, West and East Nusa Tenggara, and Papua.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Brickfields' Little India comes alive ahead of Deepavali
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Little India in Brickfields is bustling with shoppers ahead of Deepavali on Nov 8, lifting the festive mood and raising traders' hopes of stronger sales over the weekend.
A Bernama survey of the popular shopping enclave found a wide range of festive goods, from traditional clothing and footwear to accessories and sweets, drawing crowds keen to complete their preparations early.
Footwear and accessories trader Vishan Daren, 30, said recent rain had reduced footfall and affected his sales.
However, he said demand for festive essentials had picked up today, and he expected more customers on Saturday and Sunday.
"Higher prices compared with last year are among the challenges traders face, but we are still offering promotions to attract customers," he said when met today.
Meanwhile, Usha, 52, who has worked at traditional clothing shop Maharaja for nearly seven years, said the store offered a wide range of outfits, including sarees, Punjabi suits and other traditional wear, to cater to festive demand.
She said Friday to Sunday was typically the busiest period, particularly during festive seasons such as Deepavali and Hari Raya.
Usha said Deepavali also attracted customers from other communities interested in Indian traditional wear, reflecting the cultural diversity of the celebration.
"Previously, Malay customers usually bought saree fabric to make baju kurung or kebaya, but now many want to wear the saree itself," she said.
She said the festive atmosphere also brings some excitement to traders, who get the chance to interact with customers of different races and cultural backgrounds.
For Kuberakusalan, 67, from Taiping, Perak, the highlight of Deepavali is having his children return home from afar, including those working in the capital, for a family gathering.
"This year feels more meaningful because all my children and grandchildren can make it. We came here to complete our final shopping to buy some new clothes and traditional sweets to welcome them home," he said.
Fellow shopper Mullaimalar, 50, said she had only just started her Deepavali shopping due to a busy work schedule.
The Setapak resident said her shopping list included traditional sweets such as laddu and jalebi, as well as ingredients to prepare muruku and adhirasam for prayers and family feasts.
She hoped this year's Deepavali would bring happiness and good health, while instilling values of love and mutual respect within the community.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PH raises target to contest 24 seats, eyes 18 wins
Article:
AYER KEROH: Pakatan Harapan is targeting to win 18 of the 24 state seats it will contest in the Melaka election on Nov 14.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the decision to increase the number of seats from 21 to 24 was made after assessing current political developments and the coalition's ability to field suitable candidates.
He said the decision also took into account the strength of the party machinery, candidates' capabilities and acceptance among local residents.
"Initially, we had set a target of contesting 21 seats, but after looking at current political developments and the fact that some political parties had not filled the needs in certain areas, we felt we had the capacity to contest with candidates who had already been identified.
"We eventually decided to contest 24 state seats," he told a press conference after a PH Hi-Tea with the Melaka Media Practitioners Club (Pendika).
Also present were PKR Melaka state leadership council acting chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim, Bentong member of parliament Young Syefura Othman and Melaka Amanah chairman Datuk Ashraf Mukhlis Minghat, who is also the PH candidate for Durian Tunggal.
Adly, who is also Deputy Defence Minister, said PH was not only aiming to win 18 seats but also focused on retaining the five seats it had previously won, including Kota Laksamana, Ayer Keroh and Banda Hilir.
"Our target from the beginning was 18 state seats, and we believe we have the ability to win in these 18 seats while working to retain the five seats we already hold," he said.
On the possibility of overlapping candidates with Bersatu, Adly said PH was focusing on strengthening the coalition internally.
He said PH had no control over other parties' decisions to field candidates in particular constituencies, as each party had its own considerations and strategies.
He also denied that the decision to contest 24 seats was due to failed negotiations with any coalition, stressing that it was based on PH's own strategy and capabilities.
"Under any circumstances, we cannot control other parties from fielding candidates. What we can control is our own position within PH.
"We know that through this approach, we have greater potential to focus on securing victories for our candidates.
"There is no question of that (failed negotiations). Whether negotiations took place, succeeded or failed, that will depend on the outcome on Nov 14," he said.
Earlier,
Bersatu announced
eight candidates for the Melaka polls, setting up straight or multi-cornered contests with PH in four state constituencies: Ayer Keroh, Klebang, Gadek and Pengkalan Batu.

Title: Zetrix AI's RM2bil sukuk rating slashed to near-default category
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has slashed its rating on Zetrix AI Bhd's RM2 billion Islamic medium-term notes to CIS from BB+IS, citing an unresolved covenant breach, mounting financial claims and worsening governance concerns.
The rating remains on MARCWatch Negative, signalling heightened uncertainty over the group's ability to meet its financial obligations and resolve the issues surrounding thd RM2 billion sukuk.
The downgrade follows an earlier cut on Oct 16, when MARC lowered the rating to BB+IS from AA-IS.
The latest assessment reflects continued uncertainty over Zetrix AI's compliance with a covenant requiring founder Wong Thean Soon to remain the group's single largest shareholder.
A sukukholders' meeting on Oct 23 ended without a resolution, leaving the covenant breach unresolved and no indulgence obtained from investors.
MARC said this exposed the sukuk to the risk of an event of default being declared.
Although a dissolution event has been triggered, it does not automatically require immediate full repayment of the outstanding sukuk.
The rating agency also flagged mounting pressure on the group's liquidity amid growing financial claims.
Reports indicate the government is pursuing legal action to recover RM314 million in revenue allegedly collected on behalf of the Road Transport Department but not remitted.
Zetrix AI has said it has not yet received official notification from the government.
Separately, its wholly owned subsidiary MY EG Sdn Bhd received an additional RM353.1 million income tax assessment from the Inland Revenue Board.
The group has appealed the assessment.
MARC also highlighted uncertainty over the availability and liquidity of Zetrix AI's reported digital assets, which may affect its ability to meet funding requirements.
Governance weaknesses have further compounded concerns, as the group has yet to appoint new external auditors following the departure of its previous auditors.
All three members of its audit committee have also resigned.
The absence of external auditors and an audit committee removes key financial reporting oversight, raising questions over the reliability and timeliness of disclosures, the rating agency said.
MARC will monitor developments, including engagement with sukukholders and appointments to the audit committee and external auditor positions.
Should Zetrix AI fail to pay any amount due under the programme on time, the rating will be downgraded to DIS, indicating a default rating.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 112 rural projects face RM259.5mil payment arrears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Outstanding payments to contractors and compensation to landowners totalling RM259.503 million for 112 projects remained unpaid as of Sept 30, said Umno Youth executive council member Fadzmel Fadzil.
Fadzmel, who is also the press secretary to the Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, said the arrears had affected small contractors, including Bumiputera contractors, who had yet to receive payment despite completing the work.
He said the outstanding payments were carried forward from previous years, involving projects that had already started but remained unpaid.
Dismissing claims that the Rural and Regional Development Ministry had overcommitted financially, Fadzmel said the arrears stemmed from previous years and were not the result of new spending commitments.
He said a Finance Ministry (MoF) letter dated Sept 10 had directed spending control measures, including the postponement of allocations that were approved.
"What many people do not know is that the letter clearly instructed spending control measures. Not a single sen was provided to settle the arrears, while allocations that were approved were ordered to be postponed.
"That is why we want MoF to answer: until when will the postponement last? A postponement without a date is effectively a cancellation," he said in a Facebook post.
Fadzmel said the ministry was now forced to use its existing internal allocations or current financial year funds to settle the arrears.
This, he said, meant diverting funds from other development programmes and projects meant for rural communities.
Among those affected were RM200 million allocated for the construction and repair of houses for the poor, including Orang Asli communities, as well as assistance for B40 entrepreneurs.
The assistance included funding for fishermen to buy boat engines and farmers to acquire machinery.
He also challenged the former finance minister to provide evidence that the ministry had been instructed to use allocations from other ministries to settle the arrears.
"Please provide the evidence. So far, the ministry is still using Letters of Authority to Spend, drawing from its internal allocations. But if MoF is willing to provide the funds, Alhamdulillah," he said.
He added that all approvals and expenditure commitments for rural development projects were subject to MoF and Economy Ministry approval, while the Public Works Department served as the implementing agency.
On rural road projects, Fadzmel said the tender process for 40 projects under the Rural Road Development Programme, worth RM5.14 billion, had been cancelled.
Another 87 projects worth RM8.10 billion had their Letters of Acceptance (LOA) postponed.
He said the affected projects included roads in Sabah and Sarawak.
Fadzmel maintained that Zahid had not misrepresented the issue, saying the ministry had acted in accordance with government financial procedures.
He said rural roads were vital to communities in Sabah, Sarawak and the peninsula, and should not be turned into political ammunition.
He added that the ministry would explain the matter during engagements in Melaka over the next two weeks and in Sarawak.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak doubles Unimas medical intake to produce more local doctors
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak will double the intake of new medical students at Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (UNIMAS) from 40 to 80 as part of efforts to produce more local doctors and address the state's shortage of medical personnel.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg said the move was part of the state government's long-term efforts to address a shortfall of more than 1,000 doctors.
He said the decision to increase the intake was discussed with Unimas vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Dr Ahmad Hata Rasit yesterday to strengthen the university's capacity to produce more doctors.
The state government would prioritise the enrolment of Sarawakians through Yayasan Sarawak sponsorship to ensure more local students had the opportunity to pursue medical studies, he said.
Abang Johari said the shortage had become more pronounced as some doctors offered postings in Sarawak, particularly those from the peninsula, failed to report for duty.
This had made it difficult to fill vacant positions, he added.
"So, we need to produce doctors from among Sarawakians so that they can serve in their home state," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the 33rd YAB Premier of Sarawak Special Awards and Sarawak Education Awards 2026 ceremony at Hikmah Exchange Event Centre here today.
Abang Johari said the state government needed to take a more proactive approach by increasing the number of locally trained doctors rather than continuing to rely on medical personnel posted from outside Sarawak.
In a related development, he said the state government was also planning to introduce a medical programme at Universiti Teknologi Sarawak (UTS) in Sibu.
However, he said the proposal was still at the preparatory stage and required further assessment to ensure the programme met academic standards and international benchmarks.
Preparations would include recruiting qualified lecturers, providing teaching facilities and establishing collaborations with other universities with recognised expertise and standards, he said.
"If we want to implement it, at least two years will be needed for preparations, including securing teaching staff and meeting the required international standards," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malakoff files RM700mil green sukuk for Melaka WTE plant
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malakoff Corp Bhd has lodged a RM700 million green sukuk programme to part-finance the development of a waste-to-energy (WTE) facility in Sungai Udang, Melaka scheduled for completion in 2029.
Its subsidiary Sungai Udang WTE Sdn Bhd, lodged the 30-year Asean Green Sustainable and Responsible Investment sukuk Wakalah with the Securities Commission.
The sukuk received a preliminary long-term rating of AA-IS from MARC Ratings Bhd, with proceeds earmarked for the facility's development, design and construction.
The project is being developed under a 34-year concession, which took effect on June 18.
Sungai Udang WTE is 60 per cent owned by Malakoff, while the remaining 40 per cent is held by Alam Flora Environmental Solutions Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Alam Flora Sdn Bhd.
Upon completion, the facility will be Melaka's first WTE plant, capable of processing up to 1,056 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily and generating 22.1 megawatts of gross renewable energy.
It is expected to divert more than 300,000 tonnes of waste from landfills and prevent about 75,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually, helping ease pressure on the state's existing landfill as it approaches capacity.
Malakoff group chief executive officer Syahrunizam Samsudin said the project will strengthen the group's environmental solutions business while complementing its power generation operations.
He said converting waste into energy would reduce landfill waste and methane emissions while supporting Malaysia's transition towards more sustainable waste management.
The government has outlined plans to develop 18 WTE plants nationwide.
Syahrunizam said the Sungai Udang project will contribute towards Malakoff's target of expanding its waste management capacity to 10,000 tonnes daily by 2031.
He added that Malakoff's previous sustainable sukuk issuances through Malakoff Power Bhd in May 2025 and April 2026 were oversubscribed 10.34 times and 4.5 times respectively, reflecting investor confidence in the group's business.
RHB Investment Bank Bhd is the principal adviser, lead arranger and lead manager for the sukuk programme.

Title: Ringgit extends rally against US dollar as traders reassess Fed rate hike prospects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit extended its gains to close higher against the US dollar on Friday as traders reassessed the possibility of an interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve (Fed), an analyst said.
The Fed decided to keep the benchmark interest rate steady at 3.75 per cent to 4.00 per cent on Oct 28.
At 6pm, the ringgit rose to 4.0555/0600 against the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0575/0620.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the dollar-ringgit was seen to be at around RM4.0425 during the morning session but later moved towards RM4.0577, giving a 0.05 per cent gain against the dollar.
"It appears that traders are reassessing the likelihood of a rate hike, which has led to lower US Dollar Index (DXY) by 0.32 per cent to 101.710 points," he told Bernama.
Against major currencies, the ringgit eased against the British pound to 5.4461/4522 from 5.4009/4069 at Thursday's close, slid against the euro to 4.5413/5464 from 4.5176/5226, and weakened vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5782/5812 from 2.5685/5715 previously.
The ringgit was also mostly lower against its Asean peers.
It gained vis-a-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 223.4/223.8 from yesterday's close of 223.7/224.0, but slipped against the Singapore dollar to 3.1753/1791 from 3.1665/1702 previously.
It also lost against the Thai baht to 12.0373/0561 from 12.0165/0345 at Thursday's close, and inched down vis-a-vis the Philippine peso at 6.36/6.37 from 6.35/6.36 previously.

Title: IGB Reit's Q3 net profit rises to RM144.15mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IGB Real Estate Investment Trust (IGB Reit) posted a higher net profit of RM144.15 million for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026), from RM95.62 million in the corresponding quarter last year.
Revenue rose to RM249.33 million from RM165.19 million in Q2 2026.
For the cumulative nine months ended Sept 30, 2026 (9M 2026), IGB Reit's net profit increased to RM446.23 million from RM294.70 million, and the revenue also grew to RM751.62 million from RM496.72 million in the previous corresponding period.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the company said that the higher total revenue, net property income and profit after taxation were mainly due to the additional income and profit contributed by Mid Valley Southkey Mall (MVS), as well as the higher rental income from Mid Valley Megamall (MVM) and The Gardens Mall (TGM).
IGB Reit said that the three established shopping malls continue to demonstrate resilience, supported by high occupancy, positive rental reversions and strong tenant demand.
"The portfolio's strategic locations, loyal customer bases and diversified tenant mix provide a solid foundation for sustained performance," it said.
IGB Reit said it will continue to focus on proactive leasing, optimising the tenant mix, implementing asset enhancement initiatives, and managing costs prudently to keep its malls competitive.
"Despite challenges across the broader retail sector, IGB Reit remains well positioned to generate sustainable rental income and maintain stable distributions to unitholders," it added.
